title: Fundamental Rights: Doctrinal Foundations
description: Analytical overview of the structure, scope, and enforceability of fundamental rights under Nepal's Constitution.

sections.title: Conceptual Framework
sections.content: Fundamental rights constitute justiciable guarantees that structure the relationship between the individual and the state. They operationalize constitutionalism by limiting arbitrary power and articulating normative commitments to equality, dignity, and participation.

sections.title: Classification & Clustering
sections.content: Rights may be grouped functionally: civil-political (speech, assembly), socio-economic (health, education), group-differentiated (women, marginalized groups), and procedural (due process, access to justice). Such clustering aids doctrinal analysis and comparative evaluation.

sections.title: Enforcement & Limitations
sections.content: Judicial remedies (including writ jurisdiction) provide enforcement architecture. Limitations must satisfy tests of reasonableness, proportionality, and legitimate aim. The interface between directive principles and enforceable rights shapes interpretation in socio-economic claims.

summary: Fundamental rights are enforceable constraints on state power.
learningObjectives: Relate directive principles to socio-economic adjudication
